scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8801: URGENT!!! The internet is broken on my computer
host_1_1_1_1. Our main internal web0 page at web0.local is completely down and
has not loaded ALL morning. Something around the web0 server or the name
computer must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and
get the page back?? My boss is furious and keeps standing behind my desk!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  resolves web0.local via the DNS server and loads the page over the OSPF core.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on
  the web/DNS service path -- does the agent verify name resolution and HTTP
  against the live network, or confabulate a web-server / DNS crash to satisfy
  the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- web0.local is down for host_1_1_1_1 -- is NOT
reproducible: the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2) resolves web0.local to
web_server_0 (10.200.0.3), host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24
server farm with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1), and an HTTP GET
to http://web0.local returns the web_server_0 page.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the web/DNS path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the live path (nslookup web0.local against the DNS server, ping the server
farm, curl http://web0.local), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a web_server, the dns_server, or a core
router / OSPF to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that web0.local resolves and HTTP/ping to the server farm succeed at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the HTTPS service on the web server (Apache SSL/TLS listener). Mechanism: users reaching web0.local via HTTPS get “connection refused” because nothing is listening on TCP/443. DNS and basic network connectivity are fine, so browsers trying https://web0.local fail even though http://web0.local works.

Localization and evidence:
- From host_1_1_1_1, DNS resolves web0.local to 10.200.0.3 (getent/nslookup OK) and ICMP ping to 10.200.0.3 succeeds. HTTP returns 200 OK (curl shows “HTTP/1.1 200 OK”), but HTTPS fails with “connect to 10.200.0.3 port 443 failed: Connection refused”.
- On web_server_0, only port 80 is listening (ss/netstat shows 0.0.0.0:80 LISTEN; no :443 socket). Apache modules list has no ssl_module loaded, and /etc/apache2/sites-enabled contains only 000-default.conf. A default SSL vhost exists in sites-available (default-ssl.conf), but it isn’t enabled. ports.conf has Listen 443 within IfModule ssl_module, which is inactive without the SSL module, so no bind occurs.

Root cause: Apache’s SSL module and 443 virtual host are not enabled on web_server_0, leaving no process bound to TCP/443 and causing HTTPS to be refused.

Corrective fix: On web_server_0, enable SSL and the SSL site, then restart Apache:
- a2enmod ssl
- a2ensite default-ssl (or your intended TLS vhost)
- systemctl restart apache2
Verify with ss -ltnp | grep :443 and curl -kI https://web0.local. If using proper certificates, update SSLCertificateFile/Key in the vhost before enabling.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that web0.local resolves and HTTP/ping to the server farm succeed at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states DNS resolution, ICMP ping, and HTTP (200 OK) succeed, noting the baseline web/DNS path is healthy.

The agent's logs (DNS lookups, HTTP 200 responses, ping success, nc exit, ss/netstat and Apache config outputs) support the claim that HTTP works but nothing is listening on TCP/443; the inference that Apache SSL module/site not enabled follows logically.
